Size assumptions & bulk TKinteger choice

TKinteger k1–k16 follows base3_pack.py: five trits per byte, with each matrix row packed separately. Automatic scale bytes: 2 for k1–k5, 4 for k6–k16 (other quantizers: 2). Existing imported scale overrides are preserved; choose −1 to use codec widths. Input width must divide evenly by group size for the uploaded quantizer. Embedding storage can be estimated here, but the linear-only resident loader needs an embedding adapter. The separate tk_codec.py zero-float container is not this format. Tied embeddings/head are counted once. Runtime targets do not add to the weight file.

AUTOMATIC · SELECTED MODEL
What to protect during quantization.
“Precision precaution” means: consider keeping this component at its original precision because rounding errors could affect normalization, memory, routing, or output quality. It does not mean a test proved this layer is sensitive.
Conservative starting policy
This list updates automatically for every decoder block. “Protect” means exclude the listed module or parameter from low-bit weight quantization. It does not freeze training or run reconstruction.
Unchecking a group is an experiment choice, not evidence that it is safe. The a/b gates are recipe-dependent. Keep norms, decay parameters, convolutions, and routers protected in this starting policy.
    BlockModule / parameterWhy protect it?
    JSON exports the full selected policy even when search filters the table. Validate quality with your calibration data, reconstruction, and perplexity tests before reducing precision further.

    A SMALL MEMORY YOU CAN SEE
    Inside the delta rule.
    Write an association, change it, then watch the memory correct itself. This is a 2 × 2 teaching example, not a model simulation.
    1. Set the controls
    Keys A = [1, 0], B = [0, 1]. Queries use the current key, with 1/√2 scaling.
    2. Inspect the memory
    KEY × VALUE STATE S 0 tokens
    Read output: [0.000, 0.000]
    3. Follow the update
    1. DecayS̄ = α × previous S
    2. Predictprediction = S̄ᵀ × key
    3. Correcterror = β × (value − prediction)
    4. Write, then readS = S̄ + key × errorᵀ
    Try writing A twice. The second write corrects the remaining error rather than adding the full value again.
    Two kinds of memory in your model
    Batch 1. KV and convolution state at 2 bytes/value; recurrent matrix at 4 bytes/value. Tensor payload estimates only; excludes weights, workspaces, allocator overhead, and vision inputs. Sliding attention is an upper bound.

    PER-LAYER SCHEMES · ULTRAMEGA · HESSIAN MAPS
    Build the quantization run
    
 
    Choose formats inside the flow graph. Repeat-by-type applies that layer choice across matching blocks. Your head and embedding choices count toward the whole model.
    
 
    Intermediate TKinteger calculator
    Uniform k at every weight. Intermediate rates come from group size and a shared 12-bit scale. TK 1 2.2 is k1, G20, S12: 40 ternary weights plus two scales fit in 11 bytes.
    
 
    K1 always has three codes per group. Smaller groups buy independent scales, not more ternary codes. K1 G2 with FP16 scales is about 9.6 bits/weight; G1 is 17.6, before row padding and headers. G1 with FP32 scales is 33.6 bits/weight before padding and headers. There is no universal K1 storage maximum, and higher storage cost does not guarantee better model quality. Fixed S12 log-scale mapping: zero, or 2⁻³² through 2¹⁶. This scale codec is experimental. Headers are additional; partial groups are padded.
    
 
    NanoQuant-style factorization
    Binary: official NanoQuant ADMM initializer. Ternary: experimental adaptation. Both use Hessian preconditioning, block STE reconstruction and scale-only teacher KL tuning. Each layer can use a different method and rank. Quality must be measured after packing.
    
 
    Calibration & reconstruction
    
 
    Context carry is required. Chunked Hessian capture and evaluation pass the complete native cache: DeltaNet recurrent and convolution states, attention KV caches, and position history. Reset occurs at document boundaries. Block reconstruction and teacher KL process complete documents. A cached-vs-full forward check must pass before quantization.
    
 
    The executable runner supports selected Linear and Embedding matrices. Unsupported selected operations, convolution tensors or fused expert groups fail preflight; original/protected tensors remain included in saved storage. It loads the full model: runner RAM/VRAM must fit the model and working tensors. Binary/ternary reconstruction is an adapted pipeline, not a claim of published NanoQuant quality.
    
 
    GitHub Actions
    
 
    Install the supplied workflow at the repository root in .github/workflows/atlas-quant.yml. Use Save plan & start run below, or download/commit the plan and use the command. Each launch saves a new snapshot without overwriting earlier plans. Quantization uses your self-hosted Linux GPU runner with label gpu. No access token is stored in Atlas.
    
 
    The token needs access to the selected repository, with Contents and Actions read/write. It is sent only to api.github.com, never saved, and cleared after the request. This button commits a new plan snapshot and requests a GPU run. The browser cannot reuse your ChatGPT GitHub connection.
